summary: A colour chosen by a person — a brand accent, a label, a chart series — as a hex field with a swatch button that opens a saturation and brightness area, a hue strip and any preset swatches, taking and returning `#RRGGBB`.
useWhen: the colour is the user's to choose: a workspace's brand accent, a label's or a tag's colour, a series in a chart they own
any colour should be possible, not only a list — with the likely ones offered as `swatches`
the value is stored and shown back as a colour, not as a name

useInstead.when: the choice is among a few named colours and nothing else is allowed
useInstead.why: an open picker invites a colour the product then has to refuse; radios name each choice and allow no other

useInstead.when: the colour marks a status — failed, running, healthy
useInstead.why: status colours are the system's, each with a word and a shape beside it; a picked colour carries neither, and means nothing to the next reader

useInstead.when: the choice is a theme — light, dark, the system's
useInstead.why: a theme is a named mode with every colour decided; a picker would ask for one colour and leave the rest to chance

composition.note: One field. `value` is `#RRGGBB`; `onChange` fires on every step of a drag, `onChangeEnd` once a change is finished — save or recompute there. Offer the likely colours as `swatches`, each with a `label` when it has a name people use. When text will sit on the colour, check the pair yourself and pass `isInvalid` with an `errorMessage` that gives the ratio.
composition.example: <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" description="The Approve button in approval emails." value={brand} onChange={setBrand} swatches={[{ value: '#0B5FFF', label: 'Northwind blue' }]} />

sm.use: dense forms, a colour in a table row

description.note: where the colour is used, and any rule it must meet; replaced by `errorMessage` while the field is invalid

labels.note: the swatch button's name and the presets' group name

requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered
a `label` on every swatch that has a name people use — "Northwind blue" says more than "vibrant blue"
guarantees: the hex is a text field named by the label, typed and committed on Enter or blur; shorthand such as `f00` is accepted as typing and expanded, and anything that is not a colour goes back to the last one
the swatch button is named by `labels.picker`, not by the field's label, and opens a modal dialog named by the field's label, with focus in the area
the area is a two-dimensional slider: the arrow keys move saturation and brightness, Page Up and Down take bigger steps, and each step is announced with the colour's name
the hue strip is a slider named Hue, in the reader's language; in a right-to-left locale it runs from the right and the arrows follow it
presets are one radio group named by `labels.swatches`: the arrow keys move and pick, the chosen one is ringed as well as coloured, and a colour off every preset leaves none checked
a preset with no `label` is named by its colour in the reader's language
Tab moves from the area to the hue strip to the presets and stays in the dialog; Escape or a click outside closes it and focus returns to the button
the hue is kept at a grey or black: dragged to black and back up, a blue comes back blue
a caller that does not take the change keeps its value, and the field shows it
in forced colours the chip, the swatches and the thumbs keep their colours; their edges and the chosen ring take the system's
a name, `rgb()` or shorthand passed as a prop throws with the prop's name, rather than rendering an empty field
`name` posts the hex with the form
notes: No alpha: a translucent colour looks different on every ground it lands on. Ask for a solid one.
No contrast check: the picker cannot know what goes on the colour. When text sits on it, measure the pair and say so with `isInvalid`.
The colour names are React Aria's, and follow the locale.

antiPatterns.why: a value the picker cannot show as it came would come back different, and the form would read as edited the first time it was saved
`onChange` fires on every pixel of a drag — dozens of saves for one gesture, answered out of order

antiPatterns.dont: a brand colour taken with no check when white text will sit on it
antiPatterns.do: measure the pair, and `isInvalid` with "Too light for white text: 2.1:1. Needs 4.5:1."
antiPatterns.why: the picker offers every colour, and half of them make the text on them unreadable

antiPatterns.dont: a ColorPicker for an interface colour — a button's, a status's
antiPatterns.why: interface colours are chosen once, in the design system, and checked there; a picker hands that decision to whoever has the settings page open
